knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The position and the route to it form part of the height task. The top step is not a standing place, and the ladder rating is only one of the checks.
Falling through an opening or a surface that cannot bear weight is one of the main routes. The other options are not elevated work.

Trigger figures are set by jurisdiction and by the rule being applied. The Australian rule must be checked, and a foreign figure is not evidence of it. Australian law does set some heights for specific rules, such as the NSW construction rule.

practicalCriteria: Lists every elevated position and its route for a supplied job sheet, with the fall type for each
States the trigger rule used and leaves out any state figure without a source
Names at least three falling-object risks and the control for the area below each one
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Hazard entry or job plan produced for a supplied scenario
Assessor observation of the scenario answer
stopWorkCriteria: A position with a possible fall and no control in place means the scenario is not started
An untested trigger figure used as an Australian rule means the entry is returned
